messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward-devel] RKWard 0.5.0c is released
messages.body_plain:
On Mon, 2009-03-30 at 22:11 +0200, Thomas Friedrichsmeier wrote:
> Hi!
> 
> I have just uploaded RKWard 0.5.0c. For a more elaborate announcement, see 
> http://rkward.sourceforge.net/ .
> 
> Many thanks to all testers and contributors. The amount of testing and 
> feedback in the few days since my first call for testing has been truly 
> amazing.

I just updated the RPMs for Fedora (rawhide (Fedora 11) will be update
to date from tomorrow, Fedora 9 and 10 will be after a week in the
testing repository)

Sorry for not having be able to participate to the testing of this
release earlier, everything went fine for me (build and first testing).

Thanks for the new release,

Regards,

Pierre

messages.subject: [rkward-users] newest version crashes on FC10 almost immediately...
messages.subject_clean: [rkward-users] newest version crashes on FC10 almost immediately...
messages.body_plain:
Dear Developers--

A recent update to V. 0.5.0c on Fedora while using R-2.8.1 is unstable
from the earliest usage attempt.  A simple 'update.packages()' attempt
causes rkward to crash with the following error: rkward: symbol lookup
error: rkward: undefined symbol: _ZNK7QString11lastIndexOfER7QRegExpi.
 Other commands also cause a similar immediate app failure.

TIA,

-- 
Vince Fulco, CFA, CAIA
612.424.5477 (universal)
vfulco1 at gmail.com

messages.body_plain:
Hello Richard,

in the past I have used another approach for building rkward 0.4.9a
against newer versions of R that lack Rdevices.h:

    sed -i '/^#include "Rdevices.h"/d' rkward/rbackend/rembedinternal.cpp

i.e. I just removed the inclusion of Rdevices.h, with no known (to me) side effects.

Johannes

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

On Friday 24 April 2009, Richard Bair wrote:
> I'm configuring rkward with...
>    /configure --with-extra-libs=/usr/local/lib/R/lib
> --with-extra-includes=/data/download/src/R-2.9.0/src/include/

that line got you a mix of two (or possibly more) different versions of R, and 
that is the cause of the trouble. I agree the configuration is not quite 
self-explaining, when you have more than one version of R installed.

Most of the time, the --with-r-home is all you need in those cases. Probably
	./configure --with-r-home=/usr/local/lib/R
in your case.

Try that first, and write back, if it does not work for you.

Johannes' suggestion may also work, but in your case will likely leave you 
with other problems. That trick is no longer needed in RKWard 0.4.9a.

(Configuration is - slightly - less obscure in the KDE 4 branch of RKWard).

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] Preview releases of RKWard 0.4.9b and 0.5.0d
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

A month ago, we've released of RKWard 0.5.0c to address some of the more 
important bugs. We were in a bit of a hurry, then, as we hoped to get 
included in a feature of a large German computer magazine (unfortunately that 
did not work out). Due to that hurry, a number of further known bugs were not 
addressed in 0.5.0c, and we did not release a KDE 3 version at that time.

Time to address that: I've uploaded initial test releases of both RKWard 
0.4.9b for KDE 3 and 0.5.0d for KDE 4 at 
http://rkward.sourceforge.net/temp/rkward-0.4.9b-test1.tar.gz and 
http://rkward.sourceforge.net/temp/rkward-0.5.0d-test1.tar.gz respectively. 
The focus in both releases is on bugfixing (which is why I'm still not 
increasing the version number), but for the KDE 3 branch this is also the 
first time that Meik's set of plugins on item response theory is made 
available in a release.

To make sure the upcoming official releases are as solid as possible, I'd like 
to ask you to download and test either version (or of course both, if you can 
test on both KDE 3 and KDE 4).

-- Testing --
The first round of testing will be open for one week, until Wednesday, May 3. 
Please try to provide your feedback until that day. Please mention each and 
every issue that you find, even if it might have previously been mentionend 
on this list or elsewhere.

Depending on the outcome of your testing, we will then decide how to proceed.

-- Translations --
Since these are bug-fix releases, existing translations should not need any 
(substantial) updates. Of course you may want to use this opportunity to make 
some adjustments, or even to start a translation for a new language.

-- (Plugin) developers --
Please don't add any new features until the releases are done, or only after 
prior discussion on the -devel list. SVN will be open to feature additions 
once the releases are out, officially.

Regards
Thomas
